title: Five Essential Classics
description: This set of five reviews brings together films that won the Oscar for Best Picture and remain fundamental references in cinema.

slides.title: Parasite (2019)
slides.alt: Scene from Parasite - the Kim family in front of the Park mansion
slides.observation: Genre-bending satire turned thriller, and the first non-English-language Best Picture winner.
text: The Kims, a struggling family living in a semi-basement in Seoul, scheme their way into the household of the wealthy Parks: son Ki-woo becomes the tutor, then sister, father and mother infiltrate one by one through forged credentials and staged coincidences.
Their plan unravels on a stormy night when the long-hidden secrets of the Park mansion's former housekeeper surface, dragging both families into a violent confrontation with radical consequences.

slides.title: Moonlight (2016)
slides.alt: Scene from Moonlight - young Chiron at the beach
slides.observation: A triptych of identity told in three acts, from 'Little' to his encounter with the sea.
text: Chiron grows up in Miami as 'Little', a quiet boy raised by a struggling, drug-dependent mother; he finds lessons in strength with Juan, a local dealer who takes him under his wing.
In adulthood, a late-night call from his childhood friend Kevin forces Chiron to face who he has become and revisit the beach where his story began.

slides.title: Schindler's List (1993)
slides.alt: Scene from Schindler's List - the list of names
slides.observation: Spielberg's monochrome epic about a ruthless industrialist's redemption, winner of 7 Oscars.
text: In Kraków during the German occupation, Oskar Schindler runs an enamelware factory staffed by Jewish workers the SS sees as cheap labor — and profit is all he seems to care about.
As the Holocaust intensifies, he spends his entire fortune bribing officials to protect 'his' workers, ending the war penniless but with over a thousand lives saved.

slides.title: Casablanca (1942)
slides.alt: Classic scene from Casablanca - Rick and Ilsa at the café
slides.observation: Three Oscars and the line 'Here's looking at you, kid' — the archetype of wartime romance.
text: Rick Blaine, an exiled American running a nightclub in Vichy-controlled Casablanca, reencounters Ilsa, the woman who left him in Paris — now married to resistance leader Victor Laszlo.
Caught between his old love and his conscience, Rick must decide whom he helps escape to Lisbon, and at what personal cost.

slides.title: On the Waterfront (1954)
slides.alt: Scene from On the Waterfront - Marlon Brando at the dock
slides.observation: Brando's 'coulda been a contender' moment — eight Oscars and a landmark of method acting.
text: Dockworker Terry Malloy watches his brother get silenced by the mob-run union that controls the New York waterfront, where intimidation and kickbacks rule the docks.
Pressed by the parish priest and his own guilt, Terry risks everything to testify — and faces the gang on his own terms.
